# Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Turkey, 2024: initial evidence note

I used 7 web calls and stopped. This separates 2024 events from background context and keeps only claims that are directly supported by the source.

## 2024 Events

- **[Turkey's Erdogan signs off on Sweden's NATO membership](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/turkeys-erdogan-signs-off-on-swedens-nato-membership-ratification-3283398)** — Reuters, 2024-01-25. Claim: Erdoğan completed Turkey’s approval of Sweden’s NATO accession, ending a long delay and clearing a major foreign-policy hurdle. This is a favorable data point for diplomatic effectiveness and alliance bargaining. IDs: `8B.*`

- **[Press Release on Interest Rates (2024-28)](https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/en/tcmb%2Ben/main%2Bmenu/announcements/press%2Breleases/2024/ano2024-28)** — Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye, 2024-05-23. Claim: the central bank kept the policy rate at 50% and explicitly cited sticky inflation, weak domestic-demand adjustment, and geopolitical risks. This supports a mixed reading: disciplined anti-inflation policy, but also persistent macro stress. IDs: `8B.*`

- **[In setback to Turkey's Erdogan, opposition makes huge gains in local election](https://apnews.com/article/8adc4df56cdbce24f78900e1d142ff21)** — Associated Press, 2024-03-31. Claim: Erdoğan suffered a major electoral defeat as the opposition held Istanbul and Ankara and won the nationwide popular vote. This is strong critical evidence about public support and governing performance in 2024. IDs: `8B.*`, `7A.*`

- **[Consumer Price Index - December 2024](https://veriportali.tuik.gov.tr/Bulten/Index?dil=2&os=wtmbloozowcj&p=Consumer-Price-Index-December-2024-53621)** — TURKSTAT, 2025-01-03, reporting 2024 year-end data. Claim: annual CPI inflation was 44.38% in December 2024. This is critical evidence that cost-of-living pressure remained severe at year-end. IDs: `8B.*`

- **[Annual Gross Domestic Product, 2024](https://veriportali.tuik.gov.tr/en/press/54187)** — TURKSTAT, 2025-09-01, reporting 2024 annual data. Claim: Turkey’s GDP grew 3.3% in 2024. This is favorable evidence that the economy still expanded despite high inflation and tight policy. IDs: `8B.*`

- **[Turkey removes two more pro-Kurdish mayors from office for links to banned group](https://apnews.com/article/3c6c33fd7fa2d86c9dc34089e6a98c9b)** — Associated Press, 2024-11-22. Claim: authorities removed two more elected pro-Kurdish mayors, raising the total ousted since October to six; critics called the moves politically motivated. This is strong critical evidence on repression and the treatment of opposition/local autonomy. IDs: `7A.*`

## Background Context

- **[Turkey](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey)** — Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, 2024-06-17. Claim: Erdoğan entered his new term with continued tight media control; the March 2024 local-election campaign remained structurally favorable to the incumbency, and the government suffered its biggest setback since 2002. This is background context for how the 2024 political environment worked, especially information control and electoral competition. IDs: `7A.*`, `8B.*`

## Bottom Line

- The year looked **mixed to negative overall**: Erdoğan secured a major diplomatic win with Sweden’s NATO ratification, and the economy still grew, but 2024 also featured a major local-election defeat, persistent high inflation, and intensified pressure on opposition mayors.
- The strongest critical evidence is the **March local-election result** and the **November mayor removals**.
- The strongest favorable evidence is the **Sweden NATO ratification** and **2024 GDP growth**.
